sections.heading: How Mid-Handicap Golfers Should Shortlist Drivers
body: Mid-handicap golfers usually need a driver that protects ball speed on imperfect contact, launches high enough to carry, and offers enough adjustability to manage the common miss. The best head is rarely the lowest-spin tour model unless contact and launch windows are already very consistent.

sections.heading: What to Avoid
body: Avoid buying only for advertised distance. A driver that adds a few peak yards but widens dispersion is usually a bad fit for a mid-handicap player. Loft, shaft profile, face angle, and forgiveness matter as much as ball speed.

faqs.question: What handicap counts as mid-handicap for this guide?
faqs.answer: This guide treats mid-handicap broadly as golfers around the 10 to 20 range, while recognizing that swing speed and strike pattern matter more than handicap alone.

faqs.question: Should mid-handicap golfers use a low-spin driver?
faqs.answer: Usually only if launch, spin, and contact are already consistent. Most mid-handicap golfers should start with a more forgiving head and tune from there.

faqs.question: Is this based on hands-on testing?
faqs.answer: No. This is a research-led buying guide based on manufacturer specifications, category comparison, and published product-positioning signals. It does not claim hands-on field testing.
